module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1003

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1003

open scoped Nat
open Filter

/--
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Infinite {n | φ n = φ (n + 1)} := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er85e] says that, presumably, for every $k \geq 1$ the equation
$$\phi(n) = \phi(n+1) = \cdots = \phi (n+k)$$ has infinitely many solutions.

[Er85e] Erdős, P., _Some problems and results in number theory_. Number theory and combinatorics. Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003.variants.Icc :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, {n | ∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 k, φ n = φ (n + i)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that for all large $x$, the number
of $n \leq x$ with $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$ is at most $$\frac{x}{\exp((\log x)^{1/3})}$$.

[EPS87] Erd\H os, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and S\'ark\"ozy, Andr\'as, _On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions_. {II}. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1003.variants.eps87 :  ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    {(n : ℕ) | (n ≤ x) ∧ φ n = φ (n + 1)}.ncard ≤
      x / Real.exp ((x.log) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1003

findings.description: The [EPS87] reference in the docstring mixes Part II's title with Part III's publication details: it gives “On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. II. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1–7.” The stated totient bound is correctly taken from Part II, Theorem 2; only the bibliography is incorrect.
findings.source_evidence: The cited Part II paper's first page identifies it as Acta Math. Hungar. 49 (1–2) (1987), 251–259 (https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-14.pdf); Theorem 2 on p. 253 states the eventual upper bound used in Lean. Pomerance's publication list (https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/) identifies Part III, not Part II, as Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 101 (1987), 1–7.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the title and the Lean statement, but correct the reference to “Acta Math. Hungar. 49 (1987), no. 1–2, 251–259, Theorem 2.”

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some problems and results in number theory (1985), pp. 66–67: https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-32.pdf

P. Erdős, C. Pomerance, and A. Sárközy, On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions. II, Acta Math. Hungar. 49 (1987), 251–259, especially Theorem 2 and its proof: https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-14.pdf
Author-hosted copy of the same Part II paper: https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/PDF/58.pdf
Carl Pomerance's publication list, entries for Parts II and III: https://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/
Erdős collected-papers archive and bibliography: https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
Erdős problem database provenance and status table: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md
review.notes: All three mathematical statements match the primary literature. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean confirmed the inferred types, proved that adding positivity of n does not change either solution set, verified that the interval condition expresses equality of all k+1 consecutive totients, and proved finiteness of the counted set for every real cutoff. Small totient values and solution counts were evaluated. The exponential denominator is nonzero, the exponent is real 1/3, and eventuality excludes problematic logarithm inputs. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings. The live erdosproblems.com/1003 page remained behind a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers; mathematical verification therefore used the cited primary papers, and the current-status check used the public Erdős-problem database, which records 1003 as open. No status discrepancy was found in the accessible sources.
